record.paper_title: Around the Gauss circle problem: Hardy's conjecture and the distribution of lattice points near circles
record.context_brief: Improve the sector-length range in Proposition 6.1
record.original_question: In Proposition 6.1, the authors prove an asymptotic formula for the number of lattice points in the annulus Γ_R whose shifted polar data satisfy θ_λ ∈ [c,d] mod 2π and r_λ ∈ I, uniformly when the sector length |d-c| is at least R^(-1/2). Can this asymptotic be proved for a wider range of shorter sector lengths than the one established in the paper?

evidence.quote: In particular, the result gives an asymptotic formula for the number of such lattice points provided the length of the sector is ≥ R1/2+o(1).
We have made little effort to optimize the range of |d − c| for which the asymptotic holds and it would be interesting to increase this range.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $R \geq 2$ be a large real parameter and consider the thin annulus
$$\Gamma_R = \{ x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : R - 1 \leq |x| \leq R + 1 \}.$$
For each lattice point $\lambda \in \mathbb{Z}^2 \cap \Gamma_R$, write its polar coordinates as $\lambda = (|\lambda|\cos\theta_\lambda, |\lambda|\sin\theta_\lambda)$, and set $r_\lambda = |\lambda| - R$ (the signed radial distance to the circle of radius $R$). 

For an interval $I \subset [-1,1]$ and an arc $[c,d] \subset \mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$ of length $|d - c|$, define
$$N(R; I, [c,d]) = \#\{ \lambda \in \mathbb{Z}^2 \cap \Gamma_R : \theta_\lambda \bmod 2\pi \in [c,d],\ r_\lambda \in I \}.$$
It is known that an asymptotic formula
$$N(R; I, [c,d]) \sim \frac{|d-c|\,|I|}{2\pi} \cdot R \qquad (R \to \infty)$$
holds uniformly in such intervals provided the sector length satisfies $|d-c| \geq R^{-1/2+o(1)}$ (equivalently, the arclength on the circle is at least $R^{1/2+o(1)}$).

Problem: Establish the same asymptotic for a wider range of shorter sector lengths $|d - c|$, i.e., extend the asymptotic to $|d-c| \geq R^{-1/2 - \delta}$ for some $\delta > 0$ (or as far below the threshold $R^{-1/2}$ as possible).
artifact.status_search_result: No published results were located that extend the sector-length range below the $R^{-1/2+o(1)}$ threshold for this counting asymptotic in the thin annulus. The authors themselves note the range was not optimized. Status appears unknown without further evidence.
